exposure: Planned birth at 39(+0)-39(+6) weeks gestation (induction of labour)
Planned birth at 39(+0)-39(+6) weeks gestation (scheduled caesarean section)
outcome: Perinatal mortality (antepartum stillbirth, intrapartum stillbirth, neonatal death)
cohort: The study included 472,520 low-risk, singleton pregnancies in Queensland, Australia, between 2000 and 2021.
finding: Planned birth at 39(+0)-39(+6) weeks in low-risk women was associated with significantly lower odds of perinatal mortality and other severe adverse neonatal and maternal outcomes compared to expectant management.
mod_finding: Reductions in the odds of adverse outcomes were greater following scheduled caesarean section than induction of labour, while induction of labour was associated with lower odds of caesarean delivery, severe perineal trauma, and shoulder dystocia compared to expectant management.
